memo.verdict: Neutral; park. The record does not progress IG Group (IGG-GB) at Triaging and does not invalidate it. It parks the case on the return, not on the gate: no D or F sits on management ((RA 3, E 1, BB 4) at B), business quality ((E 2, BB 2) at B), predictability ((RA 8, E 2, BB 4) at B) or trackability ((RA 7, E 2, BB 4) at B), so the framework's park rule does not close the case; the modal return simply falls short of the 20 percent bar. Conviction: medium on the organic case; a working hypothesis on the Underdog leg. Three re-open triggers are named: a price at or below about 1,190p, the level at which the modal path clears 20 percent a year (1,256p at the blended multiple); a CFTC outcome that leaves sports event contracts standing, which would lift the re-rating branch to about 45 percent, near-even, and make it the modal branch; or the Q3 2026 trading update (October 2026) and the 22-Oct-2026 Strategy Update together showing organic active customers still growing at a double-digit rate with over-the-counter customer income retention at 85 percent or above and a dated buyback resumption. The thesis sentence: IG Group is a chief-executive-led corporate change case in a high-quality, cyclical, regulated business, onto which a $1.3bn US acquisition has been bolted; it is compelling in its parts and not yet in its whole. At 1,305p and 8.4x earnings two years forward the shares pay nothing for the acquisition and return about 12.7 percent a year on the organic business alone; the case clears the bar only if the multiple re-rates, and that re-rating depends on a transaction closing and a US regulator's decision rather than on anything the organic business can deliver by itself.
case: - The change is internal, chief-executive-led, and has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain for the organic business. Since Breon Corcoran's appointment on 29-Jan-2024 the change has moved from resources (a new chief executive, finance director, chair, technology head and three divisional chief executives) through choices (product velocity, a marketing step-up, portfolio pruning, two guidance upgrades in 2026) into actions and the key operating metrics (organic active customers +13 percent to 314.1k; organic first trades +74 percent to 88.4k; retention in the mid-80s percent against under 80 percent in 2024), the financial statements (net trading revenue +21 percent to £588.8m; adjusted EPS +21 percent to 68.9p in H1 2026) and the sell-side's estimates (FY2026 consensus EPS +10.3 percent over the six months to 25-Sep-2026). The framework's screen rule for a corporate change case, a chief-executive change plus a guidance increase, passes twice over.

- The internal forces are A: at least seven of twelve strong and dated. The red-flag check finds one flag partly forming (empire-building: three acquisitions totalling over £1.2bn before Underdog, one already impaired, and a chief executive with a 0.34 percent personal stake in the target) and none of the others. The external forces are C and net to neutral: tailwinds from elevated volatility and the removal of the US pattern day trading rule (4-Jun-2026); headwinds from rate cuts (a 1.0 percentage-point fall in rates removes £36.6m of pre-tax profit on segregated client funds; Deutsche Bank expects interest on client funds to fall from 14.4 percent of revenue to 10.6 percent by FY27), from competition tightening at the edges (Plus500 into US prediction markets; CMC's Westpac and Revolut white-labels; Robinhood's 26m-plus funded accounts) and from disruption (Hyperliquid's perpetuals at 125x leverage outside regulation; prediction markets institutionalising); regulation two-edged, with the CFTC's treatment of sports event contracts the unresolved binary.

- 'Financial Outputs' have turned up where the market extrapolates and down where it also looks. Revenue growth stepped from -3.6 percent in FY24 to +7 percent in calendar 2025 to +18 percent reported in H1 2026; the EBITDA margin fell from 47.3 percent to 44 percent by choice as marketing rose 51 percent to £75.4m; net interest income fell 10 percent to £54.0m. EBITDA +4 percent in H1 2026 is the honest measure of organic profit momentum against adjusted EPS +21 percent; the gap (share count, lower depreciation, adjustments) is not decomposed in the inputs and is carried as the transmission's weak link and as the reason the multiple is argued on the five-year history, not the ten-year. Of the framework's four key metrics one improves (revenue growth B), one worsens (margin D), two are flat (cash conversion C; net debt C, the direction toward more debt and fewer distributions). Modal EPS growth is inside the 12 to 20 percent band over twelve months (+12.7 percent) and below it over six months (about +5 percent), eighteen months (about +8 percent) and three years (+10.7 percent a year).
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, at its strongest: IG is a volatility-geared, rate-geared broker at the top of both cycles, whose chief executive has reinvested a windfall into marketing and a $1.3bn bet on an unregulated US market. When volatility normalises and rates fall further, the organic active-customer base (314.1k, growing 13 percent) is shown to have been bought at a rising cost, the margin falls below the mid-40s, and the shares re-rate to Plus500's 9x on a lower earnings base, or lower if the CFTC restricts sports contracts. The evidence for it: net interest income -16 percent in calendar 2025 and -10 percent in H1 2026; marketing +51 percent for EBITDA +4 percent; European retail activity per customer -9 percent year-on-year in July 2026; Independent Reserve's goodwill impaired within a year of purchase; the risks research naming this false-friend profile (volatility masking customer decay) its "highly credible runner-up"; the market's own verdict of -28.2 percent over three months. The record concedes that H1 2026 EBITDA growth of 4 percent is the honest measure of the organic case's profit momentum and that the margin is unlikely to return to 47 percent while marketing runs at about £150m a year. It holds because the operating metrics that would show decay show the opposite (organic active customers up six consecutive quarters; retention at a record; multi-product adoption +67 percent; blended payback under six months), the rate sensitivity is bounded and partly in guidance, and at 8.4x the market is not paying for the re-rating, so the competing hypothesis is largely in the price already, which is why the modal return is D rather than F. It would win on a Q3 2026 update showing organic active customers falling toward the 270,000 alarm level, or on a CFTC ruling restricting sports event contracts.

- In its fullest form (the Written Summary's competing hypothesis as carried through the record): the two-year run of upgrades coincided with the best trading conditions since 2020 and the last of a £1.4bn buyback; the chief executive spent the windfall on marketing, on a crypto exchange he impaired within a year, and on a $1.3bn US daily fantasy business bought with about 10 percent of the equity at 8.4x and a paused buyback, with a personal stake in the target; when volatility normalises and rates fall (-£36.6m of pre-tax profit per percentage point), organic EPS stalls at about 130p, the multiple settles at Plus500's 9x on a lower base or at the five-year 10th percentile of about 6.5x if the CFTC restricts sports contracts, and the shares are worth 850p to 1,170p. The record concedes every fact in it, that the acquisition record is below the cost of capital, and that the downside is not bounded by the core at any peer multiple. It holds because the leading indicators of the competing hypothesis (retention, payback, first trades, organic active customers) are all moving against it as of June 2026, the deal's structure is performance-linked and its price under 10x earnings by the more cautious broker's count, and the market has priced the competing hypothesis in full and the re-rating branch at nothing, which is why the modal return is D and the tail is A. Where it wins: organic active customers down in the Q3 2026 update; an adverse CFTC ruling; net interest income below £55m in H2 2026.
triggers: - Re-open triggers (Written Summary Part 6): a price at or below about 1,190p (1,256p at the blended multiple); a CFTC outcome that leaves sports event contracts standing (lifting the re-rating branch to about 45 percent and making it modal); the Q3 2026 trading update and the 22-Oct-2026 Strategy Update together showing organic active customers still growing at a double-digit rate, retention at 85 percent or above, and a dated buyback resumption.

- Alarm and invalidate levels (the monitoring table): organic monthly active customers trending toward 270,000 (alarm) or falling in the Q3 2026 update (invalidate), against 314.1k in H1 2026 and a Q1 2026 base of 309,200; over-the-counter customer income retention below 85 percent (alarm), below 80 percent (invalidate); organic first trades against a 45,100 quarterly base; net interest income with an H2 2026 print below £55m (alarm), the record's modal case being inside £110m to £120m in FY2026 and not below £100m in FY2027; a full-year EBITDA margin below 43 percent (alarm), against "mid-40s" guidance and consensus of 45.8 percent for FY2026; CFTC carve-outs materially restricting sports contracts or completion slipping beyond H1 2027 (alarm), an adverse CFTC ruling restricting sports event contracts (invalidate); marketing payback lengthening from under six months (alarm).

- Underdog disclosures to come: monthly active users against 1m and registered accounts against 11m once disclosed; EBITDA tracking toward Deutsche Bank's $278m threshold scenario from a $184m annualised run-rate; the $200m earn-out determination in early 2027; the management plan's $400m 2028 and $700m 2029 EBITDA thresholds.

- Open questions the record could not close: the decomposition of adjusted EPS +21 percent on EBITDA +4 percent in H1 2026 (share count, depreciation, adjustments); Underdog's economics from daily fantasy handle to revenue to EBITDA and the charges of the earn-out and the $850m management plan; Underdog vendor lock-ups on about 33m new shares; the country count for the perimeter; the fair valuation anchor (five-year history at 8.14x median against ten-year at 10.60x median, with 9.10x conceded if the mix shifts toward the US); whether the Jersey scheme's lender-consent trigger under the revolving facility bites; the Australian class action on retail over-the-counter sales from 2017 to 2023 (no reliable estimate).

- Inputs absent from the record's evidence: the firm's live thematics file and the ticker's sidecar (so thematic momentum is a research-only reading); the track-record, lessons and Wisdom Library files (so the repeated-errors attribute is C, with two plausible fits shown for testing: buying a cheap, cash-generative UK financial on a re-rating thesis that depends on an event the market has already discounted; taking a volatility-geared earnings base at the top of a volatility cycle as the base for growth); Swissquote's fundamentals and relative-strength percentile.

- Where the record's view would change upward: a benign CFTC statement (condition two resolved); an H2 2026 that holds the margin near 46 percent with net interest income inside guide; buybacks resuming early in 2027. Downward: the Q3 update showing organic active customers falling; an adverse CFTC ruling; net interest income below £55m in H2 2026; a full-year EBITDA margin below 43 percent; a change in the company's terminology from "active customers" to "funded accounts", which the risks research flags as an early warning of obscured loss.
